name: Pieter Bronck House

dates.built: 1663 (the node's figure and the Wikipedia infobox)
dates.note: The survey's own cover states 'Date of Erection: Between 166S and 1669' -- the OCR of a figure this record does not read as certain -- and the Library's item line dates the structure 'after 1660 Initial Construction'. Wikipedia gives 1663. Three statements of one date, none edited to agree with another.

refs.title: Peter Bronck House, West Coxsackie, Greene County, NY
refs.note: The Wikipedia external-links line reads: 'Historic American Buildings Survey (HABS) No. NY-3114, "Peter Bronck House, West Coxsackie, Greene County, NY", 8 photos, 2 data pages'. The Library's item line reads 'Survey number: HABS NY-3114 - Building/structure dates: after 1660 Initial Construction - National Register of Historic Places NRIS Number: 67000012.' The data page's own header OCR is 'HABS No. W 311^'.

refs.title: National Register of Historic Places NRIS Number: 67000012 (as the Library's own item line prints it)
refs.note: Confirmed by the Wikipedia infobox, which prints the same number and adds NYSRHP No. 03905.000261 and NHL designation 24 December 1967.

survey.prepared: Historic American Buildings Survey, District 3 of New York; the cover reads 'Prepared by Washington Office'. Its stated reference is Reynolds, Dutch Houses in the Hudson Valley before 1776 -- one of this node's own four sources.

measurements.name: storey_count
measurements.note: OCR. Read as one and a half, which is what the building is and what the same forms print elsewhere as '1 1/2'. A reading, marked as one.

note: Tranche 2, the Dutch trunk in America. Two data pages and no dimensions: the whole of the survey's description is 'Brick and stone, Gable roof new slates'. Worth carrying for both nodes it serves: the surveyor recorded a BRICK AND STONE house, where hudson-valley-dutch's prose describes the rural type as stone with brick reserved for the towns.
